events.title: A proof of the Grothendieck join-meet positivity
events.summary: Attend a talk by Rui Xiong on a proof of the Grothendieck join-meet positivity using geometric Satake. The presentation will include an AI-generated video of the proof, followed by a vote on which presentation was better.

evidence.description: This experimental talk has two parts. In the first 30 mins, I'll explain our proof of the join-meet positivity using geometric Satake. In the last 20 mins, I'll play an AI-generated video of the proof. In the last few minutes, we'll vote on who did a better job: me or the AI.

events.title: Graduate Workshop Series | History, Memory, Research, and Creative Practice with Dr. Haekyoung Lee
events.summary: Explore modern Korean history, archival methodology, public history, and creative practice in this 5-part graduate workshop series. Led by Dr. Haekyoung Lee, it delves into historical connections and diasporic networks, offering insights for interdisciplinary graduate students.

evidence.description: This is a 5-part Graduate Workshop Series led by Dr. Haekyoung Lee, Professor Emerita of Theater Arts at Kookmin University. Designed for graduate students across disciplines, this series explores modern Korean history, archival methodology, public history, and creative practice.

events.title: Concert Band
events.summary: The University of Michigan's Concert Band presents "For All," a program celebrating liberation and diversity. This performance features works inspired by the USA's 250th anniversary, highlighting various communities and those who dared to think differently.

evidence.description: For its final concert of the fall semester, Concert Band performs "For All." In conjunction with the USA's 250th anniversary, this concert features works that celebrate the liberation of all people: women, LGBTQIA, Latino, African American, and those Americans that dared to think differently and seek a "more perfect union."
